Level opening and required editor plugins

Project: ForgeMCPDev, UE 5.6.1. Date: October 16, 2026.

Findings

NewMap_PCGTest.umap, NewMap.umap and TestArea.umap exist under Content/Levels. The live log records successful normal loading and a clean map check for NewMap, but subsequent asset activation for NewMap_PCGTest creates an inactive World asset rather than changing the main Editor world.

The project uses DisableEnginePluginsByDefault: true and did not enable EngineAssetDefinitions. In the installed Epic source, Engine/Plugins/Editor/EngineAssetDefinitions/Source/Private/AssetDefinition_World.cpp, UAssetDefinition_World::OpenAssets supplies the normal Content Browser level-open handler and calls FEditorFileUtils::LoadMap. That plugin is enabled by default in normal engine configurations, but the project's explicit opt-in policy disables it. This is a strong explanation for opening a World as a generic asset rather than activating a level; interactive confirmation after restart is still required.

The log also reports missing /Script/WorldPartitionHLODUtilities classes when loading Open World template HLOD assets. Its engine plugin is normally enabled by default and was likewise omitted from this project's explicit list.

Correction and preservation

Enabled EngineAssetDefinitions and WorldPartitionHLODUtilities explicitly in ForgeMCPDev.uproject, preserving its other settings and plugin entries. The pre-change descriptor and SHA-256 hashes for all three maps are stored in Saved/ReferenceCity_20261016_v1/LevelOpenRecovery/. No original map or external actor package is resaved for this diagnosis. The previous gameplay dependency corrections remain in place. Also enabled IKRig after native startup exposed a missing ik_rig_asset_query Python helper required by Control Rig's startup workflow. The helper is supplied by the installed IKRig plugin; this final dependency addition has not yet been verified in a fresh interactive startup.

Verification

A separate validation project copies the map packages, external actor packages, required project binaries/configuration, Ultra Dynamic Sky and existing city assets. Native Editor startup uses /Game/Levels/NewMap_PCGTest, NullRHI and automatic quit; output is retained in LevelOpenRecovery/MapOpenValidation.log. The original project files are checked against their pre-validation hashes. Native map loading is separate evidence from interactive double-click behavior, PIE, visual rendering, streaming performance and full city recovery.

Result: the copied NewMap_PCGTest loaded as World Type Editor, completed World Partition initialization and passed Map Check with zero errors and zero warnings. The test still logged missing Interchange import-metadata classes in sky assets; those messages did not prevent this map load. Hashes of all three original maps matched during the earlier preservation checks. During the final check, the live NewMap_PCGTest.umap and NewMap.umap files were absent; the user was creating a new unsaved world in the live Editor. No restore was performed pending clarification of whether that removal was intentional. All three copied maps still match their recorded original hashes. verification.json records this distinction. The isolated diagnostic process was closed after the map checks; its process exit code is not used as a pass criterion.

The running user Editor predates the new plugin configuration. Restart the project before testing Content Browser level activation. Keep city imports stopped until the intended live level and saved actor state have been inspected again.
